newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends firm as dlr demand dries up.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends firm as dlr demand dries up.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed slightly firmer at 482.75/483.75 per dollar Monday as demand for foreign currency dried up in an illiquid market, traders said.
"Money markets were dry. Indeed some banks had to sell dollars to get bolivars," one trader said.

Heavy dollar demand and a large auction of Central Bank monetary stabilization, or TEM, bills last week left many banks short on local currency and drove overnight interbank lending rates up to a maximum of 90 percent.
Traders said the currency rate's behavior for the remainder of the week would depend on liquidity levels and the overnight rate.

Earlier Monday Central Bank Director Domingo Maza Zavala acknowledged that the Bank's policy of using a strong exchange rate as a weapon to fight inflation may have led the bolivar to become somewhat overvalued.
But Maza insisted that the level overvaluation was not great and that there would be no sharp depreciation of the currency.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
